Phoenix audit

The key art is 2000 × 1116, and the site stretches it.

The phoenix is not an upscale: it has real detail at full size. It just meets 1920 × 1080, with 3% to spare. The trouble is that the site enlarges it up to 1.9×, and its focal point, the face, is the softest part of the image.

C

Upscale only from a native master

Upscaling is allowed only as a final delivery step from a native 2752px or larger master, for example to 3840px for 4K screens. Never as the way to reach 1920 × 1080.

Gold lines show the intended gesture: the head on the upper-right third, the near wing rising out of frame, the far wing dissolving behind the headline, and the tail curving down-right onto the Threshold. The phone version is its own composition, not a crop.

One direction

The Celestial Atlas.

v1 made the site coherent. This makes it unmistakable. The reference is one specific object: a 17th-century star atlas, engraved in gold leaf on black lacquer. Obsidian, firelight and the cosmos stay; four devices are added, and each one does a job.

I · ConstellationsProposed UI

Every species gets a star sign traced from its final form. Classified creatures show only their stars, so you see the sign of something you have not met. These were derived automatically from the current art; the final ones follow the redesigned creatures.

II · The ThresholdProposed UI

"Between worlds" becomes a literal horizon at 62% of the frame: cosmos above, lit obsidian ground below. Creatures and eggs stand on it, and the page-transition line is the same line. Creature: temporary

III · Gold engravingProposed UI

All ornament, diagrams and progress are engraved line work: orbit rings, degree marks, hatching. Richness comes from the line, not from glow. It animates only once, when it draws in.

IV · The lantern (desktop)Proposed UI

Move your pointer over the box (or the hero). Your cursor carries a faint warm light that brings hidden engravings up from the dark. It is off on touch screens and with reduced motion, and it never changes text contrast.

Creature redesign

Silhouette diagnosis (record only).

The lighting wrapper improves how the current creatures are lit, not how they are designed. In solid black, the current art shows the real problem: creatures grow by adding props, hold the same pose in every stage, and share one face.

Superseded. Creature style, identity and prompts now come from the Creature Studio art bible and briefs (branch creature-studio/art-direction): hand-painted 2D, prototypes Velynx, Mossling and Cryovant. The studies below are kept only as a record of the silhouette diagnosis. The Mossling studies conflict with its agreed identity, and Duskwing and Pyraurum are withdrawn.
  • Growth by props. Mossling's first three stages are the same blob; it only gains antlers, then trees.
  • One pose. Most species stand dead-centre, frontal or in flat profile, in every stage.
  • One face. The shared eye construction gives every species the same mascot eyes.
  • Symmetry reads as an icon. At 48px, Duskwing's later stages read as a butterfly emoji.
Rules for every redesigned creature
SilhouetteEach stage is readable in solid black at 48px and changes at least two of: proportion, primary shape, pose, number of limbs.
One signature traitA trait that runs through all four stages and grows: Mossling's sprout, Duskwing's eyespots, Pyraurum's ember.
RenderingHand-painted 2D, per the Creature Studio art bible: coloured linework, three painted values, warm key light from the upper left, cool cyan-violet rim from the right, no ground in the artwork.
Common · Verdant

Mossling: A mossy boulder that learns to walk.

Superseded · use the Creature Studio brief
PersonalityPatient, sleepy, quietly protective. Heavy-lidded eyes, a slow smile; it never hurries.
Signature traitOne sprout on its back that becomes a tree by the final stage.
Shape languageRound to square. Growth is horizontal and heavy. Drops the pig snout and antlers: it grows through anatomy, not props.

Concept studies are built from simple shapes to fix proportion, gesture and silhouette before any paid generation. Final renders follow the rules above, are delivered as 1024px transparent WebP per stage, and drop into the existing art pipeline with no code change. Estimate: about 200 Runway credits per prototype, about 600 for all three.
